CounterpartyRef.description:
A pre-resolved counterparty reference: display label + navigable target.

The Morphe compiler reads this shape only when the field is annotated
``strategy="linked-ref"``; without the hint, structural inference lowers an
object to a nested record-card instead of a link.  When an obligation names
no party, the relationship field is ``None``; a carrier always names a real
destination.
CounterpartyRef.title: CounterpartyRef

EvaluationProvenance.description:
What the pane read, and what the classifier weighed to answer it.

The rule and obligation counts are the evaluation's own receipt: a standing
is only as good as the ruleset that was bound when it was computed.

Every member is ``role="provenance"`` on purpose, and that is exactly what
makes the ``key-value`` selection at the three call sites earn its keep: the
whole block lands in KeyValuePanel's provenance tier, so a receipt reads as
the pane's footer rather than as a nested record-card competing with the data
it is a receipt *for*.  The counts are not promoted out of that tier to buy a
louder primary row — "42 rules over 17 obligations" is a claim about how the
answer was reached, which is the definition of provenance here.
EvaluationProvenance.title: EvaluationProvenance

KpiCell.description:
One card in a ``strategy="kpi-row"`` collection — the typed row contract.

Embed ``list[KpiCell]`` (or any model with these field names) in a surface view
model; the compiler lowers each cell to a promoted ``SignalCard``. ``value`` may be
textual — a non-numeric measure renders as text instead of a formatted number.
``temporal="date-time-minute"`` opts a textual timestamp into the deterministic
minute-precision display floor without changing its source value.
KpiCell.title: KpiCell

ObligationRef.description: A human label and one target in the obligation entity family.
ObligationRef.title: ObligationRef

ObligationRow.description:
One row of the obligations book.

Column order is the family's: identity, then status, then quantities, then
dates.  ``counterparty`` is a nested reference rather than a scalar, so the
``strategy="table"`` hint on the collection is load-bearing — structural
inference lowers a non-flat row to a card stack.
